target_customer: Women who rent designer dresses and accessories from other women, and lenders who earn rental income
problem: Designer clothing is expensive and rarely worn. Style Lend let members list items and rent them peer to peer, with an option for the company to handle dry cleaning.
business_model: Peer to peer marketplace taking 30 percent of rentals in the DIY option and 50 percent with the on demand service
product_category: Peer to peer fashion rental marketplace

founders.name: Lona Alia
education: Business Management undergraduate degree and MBA, institutions not named
founders.background_notes: Former model who grew up in Albania and moved to the US at 15, per a YC founder story. She was a full time entrepreneur for about 2.5 years before YC.

competitors.name: Consignment resale
competitors.what: The launch article names consignment as the alternative for high end items

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace with iOS app, payments and insurance, with logistics handled by operations.

defensibility.rationale: Local supply of listings gives a weak network effect, but listings are easy to duplicate elsewhere.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rent the Runway kept growing as an inventory based rental business. Peer to peer rivals also closed, for example Closet Collective in 2014 per Business of Fashion coverage.

market_need_then: The TechCrunch launch article gives high end dresses averaging 2155 dollars retail renting for 120 dollars a week, showing a price gap for occasion wear. No usage numbers were given.

branding.brand_signature: Pitched as the Airbnb for women's closets in launch coverage
branding.community_and_virality: Press from TechCrunch, Business Insider and the San Francisco Chronicle plus a Rank and Style interview with the founder.

brand_strength.rationale: Some national press at launch, but a descriptive name and no evidence of a distinctive identity or community.

outcome_analysis: Style Lend launched peer to peer luxury fashion rental in March 2014 and later became inactive. No shutdown notice or cause was found, so the cause of failure is not public and failure factors stay empty. Databases disagree on funding, from a 70000 total to a 1.4 million seed in 2015.
notes: Company website is not listed. The YC page lists Janete Perez as a founder, but the founder story from February 2015 has the CEO describing herself as a solo founder, so she is not listed here. The 1.4 million seed in March 2015 rests on one database (Bouncewatch). CB Insights reports 70000 in total over three rounds with Plug and Play, Social Starts and Y Combinator, and a 2018 date that looks like a data error. The 2014-03 Xconomy item is a seed headline with no amount, seen in search results only, and investors are inferred from YC participation. The cause of shutdown is not public. Competitor source is the launch article which names only consignment.
